title: Effector Vγ9Vδ2 T cell response to congenital Toxoplasma gondii infection
authors: Ling Ma, M. Papadopoulou, M. Taton, F. Genco, A. Marchant, V. Meroni, D. Vermijlen
summary: Introduces the defining TCR of the TRDV2+ subset: Vγ9Vδ2 T cells are defined by a TCR containing the gamma variable region 9 (Vγ9, TRGV9) and the delta variable region 2 (Vδ2, TRDV2), and are the major gamma-delta population of adult human blood. TRDV2/TRGV9 here are transcript-level gene-segment identities (RNA-defined V usage); Vγ9 and Vδ2 are the corresponding protein TCR chains detected by antibody/flow. The subset is TCR-activated by phosphoantigens and shows a cytotoxic effector phenotype.
quotes: A major γδ T cell population in human adult blood are the Vγ9Vδ2 T cells that are defined by the expression of a TCR containing the γ chain variable region 9 (Vγ9, TRGV9) and the δ chain V region 2 (Vδ2, TRDV2).

They express a potent cytotoxic effector phenotype and are activated and expanded in a TCR-dependent manner by microbe-and host-derived phosphorylated prenyl metabolites (phosphorylated Ags, or phosphoantigens), derived from the isoprenoid metabolic pathway

title: An Update on the Molecular Basis of Phosphoantigen Recognition by Vγ9Vδ2 T Cells
authors: T. Herrmann, A. S. Fichtner, M. M. Karunakaran
summary: Defines the hallmark TCR at the gene-segment level and the antigenic ligands. Vγ9Vδ2 T cells are ~1-5% of blood T cells and express TCRs whose gamma chains rearrange Vγ9 with JP (TRGV9JP) paired with Vδ2 (TRDV2)-containing delta chains; TRDV2 is the transcript/gene-segment identity while Vδ2 is the protein chain. These TCRs respond to phosphoantigens (PAg) such as HMBPP (microbial) and IPP (accumulating in certain tumours or aminobisphosphonate-treated cells).
quotes: Their hallmark is the expression of T cell antigen receptors (TCR) whose γ-chains contain a rearrangement of Vγ9 with JP (TRGV9JP or Vγ2Jγ1.2) and are paired with Vδ2 (TRDV2)-containing δ-chains.

These TCRs respond to phosphoantigens (PAg) such as (E)-4-hydroxy-3-methyl-but-2-enyl pyrophosphate (HMBPP), which is found in many pathogens, and isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP), which accumulates in certain tumors or cells treated with aminobisphosphonates such as zoledronate.

title: Selective Enrichment of Non-Canonical Vγ9-Jγ2 TRG Clonotypes in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma With Shorter CDR3 Loops
authors: Won Joon Oh, S. Seo, H. K. I. Chamathka, Jae-Hyun Park, Tae Jin Kim
summary: States that Vγ9Vδ2 cells are the predominant blood gamma-delta population and details the butyrophilin-dependent phosphoantigen-sensing mechanism (BTN3A1/BTN3A2/BTN2A1). Notes that at the repertoire level the Vγ9 (TRG) usage is constrained but the Vδ2 (TRD) repertoire is highly diverse — a transcript/repertoire-level statement about TRDV2-containing CDR3 sequences.
quotes: Human Vγ9Vδ2 γδ T cells, the predominant γδ T cells in peripheral blood, are innate-like lymphocytes that recognize non-peptidic phosphorylated metabolites ("phosphoantigens") through a butyrophilin-dependent manner, positioning them as key mediators of tumor immunosurveillance

Phosphoantigen sensing is mediated by the BTN3A1/BTN3A2/BTN2A1 complex: phosphoantigens bind to the intracellular B30.2 domain of BTN3A1, inducing conformational changes that are transmitted to the extracellular domains, where engagement with the Vγ9Vδ2 TCR occurs.
Previous TCR repertoire analyses have shown that the Vγ9 TCR gamma (TRG) repertoire is relatively constrained, whereas the Vδ2 TCR delta repertoire is highly diverse.

title: Impaired function of Vγ9Vδ2 T cells in frail elderly
authors: Hui Li, Xiaxuan Li, Hangyu Chen, Zhanqun Yang, Mengzhu Zheng, Yuan Xue, Yingying Yan, Jian Lin, Xuan Lai, Long Chen
summary: Summarises the effector functions of the Vδ2 subset: it is the most abundant circulating gamma-delta population and mediates direct cytotoxicity (perforin/granzymes, Fas/FasL), rapid secretion of IFN-γ and TNF-α, IL-17 production, and immunomodulatory/antigen-presenting activity. These are protein-level effector-molecule functions attributed to the Vδ2 (TRDV2) subset.
quotes: The Vδ2 subset, pairing predominantly with the Vγ9 chain to form Vγ9Vδ2 T cells, constitutes the most abundant circulating γδ T cell population in adult peripheral blood
Vγ9Vδ2 T cells exert direct cytotoxicity against target cells (e.g., tumor cells) via cytotoxic granule release (Perforin, Granzymes) or the Fas/Fas ligand (FasL) pathway.
Upon activation, they rapidly secrete key pro-inflammatory cytokines like Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-α), bolstering host defense.

title: γδ T cell antigen receptor polyspecificity enables T cell responses to a broad range of immune challenges
authors: Jing Guo, R. Chowdhury, Vamsee Mallajosyula, Jianming Xie, M. Dubey, Yuanyuan Liu, Jing Li, Yu-Ling Wei, Brad A. Palanski, Conghua Wang, Lingfeng Qiu, M. Ohanyan, Oliver Kask, Elsa Sola, Lilit Kamalyan, David B Lewis, T. Scriba, Mark M. Davis, Dylan Dodd, Xun Zeng, Y. Chien
summary: Provides tonsil-specific evidence for gamma-delta T cells: antigen-reactive gamma-delta T cells are present in tonsils, are enriched among tonsillar gamma-delta cells relative to paired blood, and expand in tonsil organoid cultures upon live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) stimulation. Their repertoire includes canonical Vγ9Vδ2 TCRs. This is functional/repertoire evidence in the same tissue (tonsil) as the atlas.
quotes: They also contained Vγ9Vδ2 TCRs with the canonical CDR3γ sequence CALWEVQELGKKIKV, generated from the Vγ9 and JγP gene segments without N-nucleotide addition, or with limited VJ junctional variations.

Cy3 + HA + γδ T cells were present with variable frequencies in the tonsils (SI Appendix, Fig. S6B) but showed higher frequencies among tonsillar γδ T cells compared to paired peripheral blood γδ T cells (Fig. 4E).
Stimulating tonsil organoid cultures with live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) induced Cy3 + HA + γδ T cell expansion when compared with unstimulated cultures.

title: Evolution and Function of the TCR Vgamma9 Chain Repertoire: It’s Good to be Public
summary: Describes the extrathymic selection and phosphoantigen reactivity of Vγ9Vδ2 (Vγ9-JP) cells and explicitly compares this monomorphic-ligand selection to that of alpha-beta innate T cells including NKT and MAIT cells — directly relevant to the atlas conflation of MAIT and TRDV2+ labels. Repertoire/selection-level (transcript-defined Vγ9-JP rearrangement) statements.
quotes: Lymphocytes expressing a T cell receptor (TCR) composed of Vgamma9 and Vdelta2 chains represent a minor fraction of human thymocytes.

While selection on a monomorphic presenting molecule may seem unusual, similar mechanisms shape the alpha beta T cell repertoire including the extreme examples of NKT or mucosal-associated invariant T cells (MAIT)
